chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who pronounced zihar from his wife five times or more; what is upon him? He said: 'Upon him, for each time, is an expiation.'

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar (a specific form of pre-Islamic and early Islamic divorce where a husband compares his wife to his mother's back, rendering her unlawful for intercourse until expiation is made)
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation (a religious act or payment required to atone for a specific violation or obligation)
key_terms.مَكَانَ كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ: For each time (indicating that each instance requires a separate expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for multiple pronouncements of zihar?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for zihar is cumulative, requiring a separate atonement for each distinct pronouncement rather than a single collective penalty. This ruling underscores the individual accountability of the act in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from cases where multiple utterances might be considered a single event. It provides a precise legal mechanism for resolving marital disputes arising from repeated declarations of zihar.
